title: Telemetry gates and Terraform health modules for VPC deployments
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) customers need explicit, upgrade-safe health checks and SLO probes that cover latency, error-rate, saturation, and token throughput across both control-plane and private workers. Current terraform modules provide basic liveness/readiness but lack unified telemetry gates and deploy-time assertions, which leads to blind spots during canary upgrades and burst traffic.

Goal: Deliver a set of Terraform-native health modules and a runtime telemetry 'gate' library that: (1) standardizes SLO probe definitions for latency, error-rate, saturation, and token throughput, (2) wires probes into existing VPC IaC so probes are deployed and configured consistently, and (3) provides automated canary/upgrade gates that prevent unsafe rollouts and enable deterministic rollback triggers for private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform modules exist under modules/vpc-health providing templated Prometheus serviceMonitors, probe-configmaps, and reconciler hooks
SLO definitions for 50/95/99 latency, 5m error-rate, worker saturation (%) and token throughput watermark are codified as policy files and versioned
Upgrade gate runs during Terraform apply/plan and fails fast when canary probe windows show regressions beyond thresholds
Dashboards and alerting rules created and documented; default runbook for triggered gates exists
Automated e2e tests simulate token surge and verify graceful degradation and fallback routing
Module config supports override for Private/Dedicated differences and includes secure defaults for metrics retention and PII-safe labels
implementation_notes: Create terraform module: sources/infra/modules/vpc-health with inputs: service_selector, metrics_endpoint, slo_bundle_version, canary_window_minutes

Implement lightweight sidecar exporter to expose token-meter and saturation metrics (ingress_token_meter, worker_kv_utilization) behind auth header; image will be private-registry/redwood/vpc-health-exporter:beta
SLO bundle format: use YAML with fields: name, metric, window, threshold, severity, remediation_hint. Store bundles in git and add CI linting
Plan to reuse existing vpc-health-exporter work from ENG-42013 but refactor to support watermark-based throttles and non-synthetic token meters
Provide a terraform 'preflight' hook that queries probe history (via metrics API) before approving an upgrade; for offline environments use exported artifacts (last-24h snapshot)
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (alpha): deploy module to 2 internal VPCs, enable exporter in sidecar mode, collect baseline metrics for 72h
Stage 2 (beta): enable Terraform preflight gate on canary channel for 5 customers with low-risk SLAs
Stage 3 (ga): enable default canary gate in terraform module, document opt-out path for emergency ops
Rollback: automatic on gate failure; manual intervention requires runbook steps and incident ticket creation
testing_plan: Unit: terraform plan/apply unit tests using terratest for module inputs and defaults
Integration: spin up a VPC cluster replica in ci/vpc-integration and run token surge harness that pushes 3x typical token throughput for 10 minutes
Chaos: simulate worker saturation by injecting synthetic KV cache latency and verify alerts and throttles engage
Upgrade-safety: run nightly upgrade simulations with canary gate enabled and assert no unsafe rollouts
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: exporter sidecar adds CPU overhead to private workers (~1-2%); accepted for improved visibility
Tradeoff: preflight gates require metric history; for heavily air-gapped customers we will accept snapshot uploads which increases operational complexity
Decision: use watermark-based throughput meters rather than absolute counters to better reflect effective token capacity under multi-tenant noise
risks: False positives from noisy metrics may block legitimate upgrades; mitigated by requiring two consecutive failed windows before aborting rollout
Secrets leakage risk from exporter endpoints; mitigated by mTLS between exporter and metrics scrapers and KMS-backed credentials
Terraform hook execution time may slow CI; preflight hooks will be optional and gated behind a feature flag
dependencies_notes: Depends on infra perf tagging work (ENG-60182) for consistent metric labels and on token-metering schema from ENG-62319. Need console dashboard templates from ENG-42013.
